COMMANDERS NARRATIVE SUMMARY

1. The Second Battalion, Fifth Marines was reactivated on 8
August 1965 at Camp Pendleton, California, after a WESTPAC
deployment which included duty in Viet Nam as Third Battalion,
Ninth Marines. On 17 December 1965 reference (c), designated
2nd Battalion, 5th Marines a BATTALION LANDING TEAM for planning
purposes. Preparation for deployment by the Battalion and
attachments commenced prior to this date. Reference (d),
activated the BATTALION LANDING TEAM on 1 January 1966.
2. The following are the major problem areas encountered from
17 December 1965 until embarkation on 9 January 1966.
A. S-1. The organization was below fifty percent deployable
strength on 17 December 1965. During the period of 20 December
1965 to 8 January 1966, the Battalion joined 534 enlisted Marines
and percentage wise, our attachments had done similarly. When
BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 embarked on 9 January 1966, the manning
level and on-board strength was as follows:

Upon debarkation and in accordance with reference (d), BATTALION
LANDING TEAM 2/5 was deactivated and the attached units were
detached to parent units on Okinawa.
B. S-2. Our present S-2 Officer and S-2 Chief were not
assigned until 3 January 1966 and 5 January 1966 respectively.
C. S-3. From 19 December 1965 until embarkation on
10 January 1966, training had been limited to MOS training,
marksmanship requalification and some field work. Of necessity,
on occasion, training took a back seat to materiel and equipment
readiness and embarkation.
3

Training aboard ship was limited to formal instruction and physical training. Formal instruction was accomplished on general military type subjects, Viet Nam orientation, and Landmine Warfare. Training began upon arrival on Okinawa on 2 February 1966, all units are accomplishing field training and field firing. Crew served weapons personnel have completed a one week organizational level school, and the majority of personnel have fired their T/O weapon for battle sights. The first rifle company is undergoing Counterguerrilla Warfare School in the northern training area which is scheduled for all units.

C. S-4. (SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND EMBARKATION)

Several items of supplies and individual equipment that were left in WESTPAC by this organization in July 1965 were missing when the Battalion received the warning order. Priorities on requisitions were upgraded by messages since they had been on order since August 1965. Priorities generated by the warning order released many of these items, but this organization was still short some items of 782 gear upon embarkation. The BATTALION LANDING TEAM had 93% of its operating stocks and 98% of its mount out. All shortages were non-essential combat equipment items. They were: Sniperscope Batteries, Suspender Straps, Tent Pins, Bayonet Scabbards, and Mess Pans. A PU-348 generator previously invoiced to REGIMENTAL LANDING TEAM-1 was replaced with a PU-239. Nineteen new M-416-B-1 trailers were received by this organization. However, due to the fact that no spare parts were available for the new trailers, both the M-416-B-1 and M-100 trailers were embarked. An additional 30 days operating stock was ordered. Eighty percent of these requisitions were filled prior to embarkation.

4 ENCLoSURE (1)
DECLASSIFIED

DECLASSIFIED

The following mount-out blocks were ordered, embarked, and in
some cases packed, which were not previously held by this
organization. These were:
    (1). 30 day class I
    (2). 30 day 1st through 3rd echelon class II spares
    (3). 30 day dry cells
    (4). 4 day class III
    (5). 30 day class IV
    (6). 30 day class V
At the time the Battalion received the warning order, the
embarkation Officer was on leave. Several minor difficulties
were encountered during the embarkation planning due to lack of
experience of the embarkation team and the relatively short notice
given. As directed by the warning order, the ships were combat
loaded. This presented numerous embarkation problems, as the
exact cargo load was not known early in the planning stages, and
was changed several times after loading plans were completed.
These changes were due to the fact that supplies back ordered for
this organization were still arriving at Camp Pendleton as late as 7
January 1966. Cargo ordered for other 1st Marine Division units
was ordered loaded on a space available basis, thereby complicating
embarkation procedures.
The BATTALION LANDING TEAM S-4 Officer and S-4 chief were left
behind to secure the camp and upon completion, flew to Okinawa to
make arrangements for our debarkation there. References (e), (f),
and (g) were sailing reports from the USS BEXAR (APA-237, USS
MATHEWS (AKA-96) and USS BELLE GROVE (LSD-2) respectively. These

COMMAND CHRONOLOGY

17 December 1965 - Reference (c) activated BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 for planning purposes.

18 December 1965 - Reference (h) directed the deployment of BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 from CONUS to WESTPAC in shipping designated by COMPHIBPAC.

18 December 1965 - Reference (i) designated the shipping required for execution of movement of BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 from CONUS to WESTPAC. The ships designated were the USS BEXAR (APA-237), USS BELLE GROVE (LSD-2), and USS MATHEWS (AKA-96).

20 December 1965 - LTCOL R.H. USKURAIT relieved Major L.W.T. WALLER II as Commanding Officer of Second Battalion, Fifth Marines. Major WALLER assumed the duties as Battalion Executive Officer replacing Major R.A. PAPE who assumed the duties of S-3 Officer.

21 December 1965 - Reference (j) issued the deployment orders for BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 from CONUS to WESTPAC.

30 December 1965 - Reference (k) directed BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 to be activated as of 010001U January 1966.

6 January 1966 - The REGIMENTAL LANDING TEAM-5 advance party departed CONUS via air transportation for WESTPAC.

6
ENCLOSURE (1)

DECLASSIFIED

DECLASSIFIED

BATTALION LANDING TEAM members on this party were:
1. Major R.A. PAPE Battalion S-3 Officer
2. 1stLt W.E. SMITH Battalion Motor Transport Officer
3. SSgt J.D. WYZSMIRSKI Property NCO
4. Corporal H.K. NOE S-1 Clerk
7 January 1966 - BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 commenced loading of
cargo at Long Beach California, for movement to WESTPAC.
8 January 1966 - Loading of cargo completed
9 January 1966 -Troops of BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 embarked on
ships.
10 January 1966 - Ships sailed from pier "E" at Long Beach, California
bound for Okinawa via Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. BATTALION LANDING
TEAM 2/5 came under operational control of Fleet Marine Force, Pacific.
18 January 1966 - BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 arrived at Pearl Harbor,
Hawaii.
20 January 1966 - BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 departed Pearl Harbor,
Hawaii, bound for Okinawa.
2 February 1966 - BATTALION LANDING TEAM 2/5 arrived in Okinawa.
Attached units aboard the USS BEXAR were detached to parent units
at Okinawa. Second Battalion Fifth Marines came under operational
and administrative control of First Marine Division (Rein).
4 February 1966 - USS MATHEWS (AKA-96) and USS BELLE GROVE (LSD-2)
arrived in Okinawa. Attached units aboard these ships were detached
to parent units.
5 February 1966 - Second Battalion Fifth Marines came under
operational and administrative control of Fifth Marines.

7 ENCLOSURE (1)
